clue.text: Growing wood destined to end up in unstarted room in church

parts.note: something bound for a place is destined to end up in it, so this phrase gives the preposition for

indicators.note: a thing not started has lost its beginning, so the first letter of the church room goes

parts.note: a vestry is the room in a church where clergy robe

explanation.surface: Someone's career path seems fated to finish in a cramped back room of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstarted' drops the V of VESTRY, leaving ESTRY. 'Growing wood' is the definition, the business of raising trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The cultivation and management of trees for timber is the craft of raising timber, so growing wood describes it exactly.

clue.text: A number of signs — about one dozen, turning

indicators.note: turning round means the run built from the next three words is read from its end backwards

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
the Roman numeral I is one
DOZ is the standard abbreviation for dozen

explanation.surface: Something with roughly twelve signs is spinning round, like a carousel of symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses CA + I + DOZ (CAIDOZ) to give the answer. The surface hints at the twelve signs, which is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The astrological band is divided into twelve signs, so it really is a set of signs.

clue.text: Plants one among drug agents and is given backing

indicators.note: one placed among the agents sits inside the word for them

parts.note: narcs is American slang for narcotics officers
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: given backing means the little word is turned so it reads from the back

explanation.surface: Drug squad officers have one of their own working among them, and he gets support.
explanation.walkthrough: NARCS is American slang that British solvers meet mostly in crosswords; 'given backing' turns the last two-letter word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils and their relatives belong to a genus of flowering bulbs, so they are plants.

clue.text: Like many blazers, tear in a low place

indicators.note: the rip is put in the pigsty, inside its letters

parts.note: a sty is a squalid, low place, a pigsty
a rip is a tear

explanation.surface: A schoolboy has ripped his blazer while messing about somewhere grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazers' are striped jackets, as worn at cricket clubs and boating clubs in Britain, not fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Club and school jackets are often made in bold bands of colour, so they are banded.

clue.text: Disreputable fellow before judge getting bad treatment

parts.note: a rough is a rowdy, a hooligan
a justice is a judge

explanation.surface: A thug goes before the bench and gets an unfair sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' just puts ROUGH first.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means punishment that is harsh or unfair, not properly handed out, so it is ill-treatment.

clue.text: Provide an excuse all in bid never to finish

indicators.note: none of the three words gets to finish, so each loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A gambler puts everything into one wager that is doomed never to be completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never to finish' cuts ALL to AL, IN to I and BID to BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, it means to give someone a claim of being elsewhere, an excuse.

clue.text: Pop music performances by daughter unlikely to fail

parts.note: rock is a kind of popular music
soli are solo performances, the plural of solo
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A band's pop gigs with a daughter on board look a safe bet.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLI is the musicians' plural of solo.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependable and firm, like stone that will not give way, so it is reliable.

clue.text: Sudden stresses giving instruction to get son out of Zion?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
the command 'S for Z' is how you get one letter in place of another, so the substitution word is the instruction
to turn Zion into son, the Z and the I are the letters that go out of it

explanation.surface: Sudden pressures come with a command to bring a boy out of the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S FOR Z AND I: put S in place of Z, take out I, and ZION becomes SON. The question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In music these markings tell players to give notes a sudden strong accent, so they are abrupt emphases.

clue.text: Space agency adopts large piece of armour

indicators.note: the agency takes the letter on board, adding it to itself at the end

parts.note: NASA is the American space agency
L is the size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The American space agency takes on a big bit of protective kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A nasal is the nose-guard on a helmet, not something to do with noses in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose-guard bar on a medieval helmet carries that name, so it is a part of armour.

clue.text: What needs a clear sun for working?

definitions.text: What needs a clear sun for working?

indicators.note: working means the letters of the phrase before it are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle: what device only works when the sky is clear and the sun shines?
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' makes an anagram of A CLEAR SUN FOR, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror device that concentrates sunlight to make heat only works on bright cloudless days.

clue.text: Take in just how many true words are spoken?

indicators.note: spoken signals the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the saying runs: many a true word is spoken in jest, so the manner of speaking is in jest

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks how many honest remarks really get made.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'many a true word is spoken in jest' supplies IN JEST, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food or drink is to take it into the body, so it means absorb.

clue.text: Rap elbow badly — it's worse than expected

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone knocks their elbow hard and finds it hurts more than they thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RAP ELBOW.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a score over the standard is a poor result, so the phrase means substandard.

clue.text: Fool, one from Northern Ireland

parts.note: one points back to fool: a twit is one, another idiot

explanation.surface: Someone is called an idiot, and from Belfast to boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for another fool, TWIT, which comes from NI.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot or silly person, a common insult for someone dim.

clue.text: Stop undercover group producing biological germ

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
a cell is a small secret group within an organisation

explanation.surface: Police halt a secret cell that is cooking up a deadly germ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'germ' here is the old sense of a seed or origin, not a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: An unspecialised cell from which other tissue develops is a biological seed of growth.

clue.text: Fine pub is European

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A good local pub is said to be European in style.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is a northern European.

clue.text: The Gunners initially rusty, especially having few matches?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following two words

explanation.surface: Arsenal, nicknamed the Gunners, look a bit rusty, especially with so few games played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Gunners' suggests Arsenal football club; here it is the Royal Artillery. 'matches' means equals, not games.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon has few things like it, few equals, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Eastern brandy produced by Soviet (not European) unknown around 54

indicators.note: the trimmed word wraps round the Roman number
not European says the letter for European is left out of the word

parts.note: LIV is 54 in Roman numerals
algebra calls its unknowns x, y and z

explanation.surface: Some mysterious spirit from the East was made by the Soviets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes E, leaving SOVIT; no anagram is needed, as 'around' simply splits it after the S to take in the Roman 54.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum spirit from the Balkans and central Europe is a brandy of eastern Europe.

clue.text: Sound of hesitation after orangeries artificially created shrub

indicators.note: the hesitation sound comes after the rearranged word
artificially created signals that the letters are rearranged into something new

parts.note: um is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone hums and haws over a bush grown in man-made glasshouses.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged greenhouses give the first ten letters; the hesitation sound is tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented pelargonium grown as a bushy plant, so it is a shrub.

clue.text: Popish Plot perjurer makes a speech dismissing king

indicators.note: dismissing the king sends that letter away from the word

parts.note: orates means makes a speech
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A perjurer gives a speech that dismisses the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates made up the Popish Plot of 1678, a supposed Catholic scheme to kill Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus of that name invented the 1678 plot and lied under oath, so he is its notorious perjurer.

clue.text: Set to value what can be said about both England and Europe, say

parts.note: the thing you can say about the two names is that each one's initial is the same letter
E is the standard abbreviation for England and also for Europe

explanation.surface: Something holds equally for England and for Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as INITIAL IS E, true of England and Europe alike; 'say' marks them as examples. 'Set to value' is a computing sense, giving a variable its starting value.
explanation.definitionFit: In programming, to give a variable or system its starting setting is to prepare it for use.

clue.text: Cold solution for washing outside of messy saddle for horse

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the washing solution goes outside, wrapping the jumbled word

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution for washing

indicators.note: messy signals that the letters of the following word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cold soapy wash is used to clean the outside of a dirty saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' looks as if it wants the outer letters of 'saddle'; instead the washing solution goes outside the jumbled saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of heavy draught animal from Scotland, so it is one kind of equine.

clue.text: Deportation on marine transport, initially, which saves one flying

parts.note: ejection is throwing out, as deportation does
marine means of the sea

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of transport

explanation.surface: Someone is deported on a ship, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the deportation word on top of SEA + T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot's catapult chair throws them clear of a crashing jet, saving their life in flight.

clue.text: Preserve hearing in jazz performance

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
a session is a sitting of a court, a hearing

explanation.surface: Some fruit preserve is offered as evidence at a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal gathering of musicians improvising together is an impromptu gig.

clue.text: Difficult situation about one good deal for gas burner

indicators.note: the situation word wraps about the next pieces

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation
the Roman numeral I is one
a lot is a good deal

explanation.surface: A tricky spot arises over one bargain for a gas cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' tempts as a bargain; here 'good deal' is simply a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The small permanent flame that ignites a boiler or cooker is the burner kept alight.

clue.text: I soon comb unruly shock in the form of a wave

definitions.text: shock in the form of a wave

indicators.note: unruly hair, like jumbled letters, is out of order

explanation.surface: Someone vows to comb unruly hair soon after a shock leaves it wavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges I SOON COMB. A 'shock' of hair is a pun: here it is a pressure wave.
explanation.definitionFit: The bang from an aircraft breaking the sound barrier is a pressure wave, a shockwave.

clue.text: Swiss dish initially served sandwiched in bread

indicators.note: the letter is sandwiched between the bread's letters

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of served

explanation.surface: A Swiss dish is first served in a bread sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S from 'served', and 'sandwiched in' puts it inside ROTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried grated potato cakes are a national dish of Switzerland.

clue.text: Primate installing saint as a feature in church

indicators.note: the ape takes the saint inside, installing it in its letters

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A primate bishop installs a saint as part of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which suits the church surface; here it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded end recess behind an altar is part of church architecture.

clue.text: Taking the floor, flowery in speech

indicators.note: taking away the floor removes those letters from the word

parts.note: floral means flowery
FL is the abbreviation for floor

explanation.surface: Someone stands to speak and their speech is flowery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the floor' suggests standing up to speak; here it means removing FL from FLORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, as an examination done by voice is.
